sentence: This project supports bioinformatic analysis that combines many kinds of data for cancer studies, including biomarker discovery and the role of epigenetics.
This project studies how mitochondria and phagosomes interact after phagocytosis and how two metabolite transporters help dendritic cells carry out immune functions.
This project tests whether artificial intelligence analysis of fat around the coronary arteries on CT exams can predict future cardiovascular events.
This project uses genomic and machine learning methods to find factors that drive opioid use disorder risk among Veterans with chronic pain.
This project studies how more DNA damage leads to muscle stem cell exhaustion in aging.
This project builds a rapid test that shows how well broadly neutralizing antibodies act on the HIV reservoir in patients.
This project studies how enteroendocrine cells form and work, and how they go wrong in obesity and type 2 diabetes.
This project studies how one protein with many roles affects biofilm formation by Streptococcus mutans and improves small molecules that inhibit it.
This project tries to find out how a protein that acts as a tumor suppressor works to suppress cancer.
This project studies how stigma over a lifetime affects alcohol use in women and their offspring.
This project uses live imaging and super-resolution microscopy in dopaminergic neurons to test whether dopamine transporter recycling and trafficking fail in Parkinson's Disease.
This project studies how a deficit of a molecule turns chronic blood disorders into acute myeloid leukemia and builds a drug to restore it.
This project studies how sensory structures of the inner ear are built and repaired after noise exposure, using mouse models.
This project builds and tests patient-derived xenograft models so studies can better represent the patients a cancer center serves.
This project uses wastewater sampling to find areas with a high burden of HIV and then works to reduce HIV in those areas.
This project tries to find out which epigenetic controls guide T cell development from hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells.
This project studies how the frontal cortex supports the ventral visual stream in the primate brain, using imaging and deep learning tools.
This project studies how sensors inside cells detect RNA viruses that copy themselves within membranes.
This project sets up a core that gives researchers instruments and methods such as mass spectrometry to study cardiometabolic disease.
This project tests whether a clinical decision support tool can raise how often older adults with diabetes are screened for cognitive impairment.
